report.summary: Chunk 5 of 6 of clones.py: implements near_clusters() and helpers (_overlap, _candidate_pairs), with comments explaining design decisions and precision notes.
risks: near_clusters | medium | The comment states that token_bag() and abstract_fingerprint() each call _abstract_tokens() internally, causing redundant work. This is a performance issue but not a correctness bug. To settle: verify whether _abstract_tokens is called twice per unit or if caching is possible.

TYPE3_EXCLUDED_LANGUAGES | medium | The comment explains that C/C++ are excluded because _GENERIC_KEYWORDS lacks C types, causing false positives. If C/C++ are added in the future, false positives may appear. To settle: check if _GENERIC_KEYWORDS covers C type system.

_candidate_pairs | low | The function uses a pair_cap to limit pairs, but the return returns early if pair_cap reached, potentially missing some pairs. This is by design. To settle: confirm that early return is acceptable for large corpora.

claims.text: This recomputed the exact fingerprint that unit_clusters had ALREADY computed for the same unit -- one full normalize per unit, wasted.
claims.why: The code calls memo.exact_fp(u) inside the loop, and the comment indicates that exact_fp was already called during unit_clusters computation. This is a performance note about redundant work.

claims.text: Multiset overlap = |A intersect B| / |smaller bag|. 1.0 means the smaller bag is fully contained in the larger; the SourcererCC similarity measure.
claims.why: The _overlap function computes inter = sum((a & b).values()) and denom = min(sum(a.values()), sum(b.values())), returning inter/denom, matching the claim.

claims.text: C/C++ were excluded by ACCIDENT until _ts_name learned to read `declarator`: every C unit was named "<anonymous>" and the _ANON filter below dropped it. Naming them removes the accident, so the exclusion has to become deliberate or it silently becomes an admission. It is not safe yet: _GENERIC_KEYWORDS has no C type system (int/char/unsigned/sizeof/typedef/struct/volatile/template/...), so C's abstracted alphabet collapses to ~16-22 symbols and unrelated functions score 0.72-0.90 pairwise -- above the 0.8 threshold. Admitting C requires extending _GENERIC_KEYWORDS plus a green false-positive suite; until then, fabricating clusters is the worse error, so C/C++ stay out and index.py REPORTS the exclusion rather than returning a silent zero.
claims.why: The claim references _ts_name, _GENERIC_KEYWORDS, and index.py, none of which are present in this chunk. The exclusion itself is defined as {'c', 'cpp'}, which is visible, but the reasoning about false positives and index.py reporting cannot be verified here.

claims.text: Bounded candidate generation over RARE (non-ubiquitous) tokens. Small corpora: all pairs. Large corpora: a SourcererCC-style inverted index token->units, so only units sharing a rare token are ever compared — the O(n^2) blow-up is never paid.
claims.why: The function _candidate_pairs checks if n <= 60, returns all pairs; otherwise builds an inverted index and only compares units sharing a rare token.

claims.text: Overlap is the SourcererCC multiset measure |A∩B| / |min(A,B)| on the abstracted bags. Union-find groups transitively similar units; each cluster carries ``similarity`` (mean pair overlap) + ``similarity_max``. Never auto-collapsed (safety-annotated) — a heuristic, advisory only.
claims.why: The claim mentions union-find, similarity, similarity_max, and safety annotations, but the code chunk only shows the function signature and initial filtering (pool, bags, afps, keep). The actual clustering logic is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: PRECISION NOTE (honest, load-bearing for the Rust port): abstracting every identifier to ``ID`` makes low-entropy code (React/JSX callbacks, thin API wrappers) look near-identical, and transitive union-find then chains such a family into one giant blob. Three guards keep the signal actionable without changing the metric: (1) inline lambdas (``<anonymous>``) are excluded; (2) a pair must share >= ``min_shared_rare`` NON-ubiquitous tokens (incidental single-token matches don't chain); (3) a cluster stops growing past ``max_cluster`` members. All three are bounds, not correctness — a Rust port must mirror them to reproduce the output.
claims.why: The claim describes guards (min_shared_rare, max_cluster) and the exclusion of anonymous lambdas. The code shows _ANON exclusion and the function parameters include min_shared_rare and max_cluster, but the actual use of these parameters is not in this chunk. The claim about Rust port is external.

claims.text: Abstract ONCE and derive both. token_bag() and abstract_fingerprint() each call _abstract_tokens() internally, so calling both here tokenized the same source twice per unit -- the single largest piece of redundant work in the clone passes. Output is unchanged by construction: the bag is the same Counter and the fingerprint comes from the same helper.
claims.why: The code calls _abstract_tokens(u.source, spec) and then uses the tokens to create a Counter. The comment notes that token_bag() and abstract_fingerprint() would each call _abstract_tokens again, causing redundancy. This is a performance observation, and the code in this chunk does call _abstract_tokens once.

observations.what: The variable 'tokens' is computed but never used in the visible part of near_clusters; it is assigned to 'bag' as a Counter, but 'tokens' itself is not used after that.
The comment in near_clusters about redundant calls to _abstract_tokens is accurate for the described scenario, but the code in this chunk only calls _abstract_tokens once per unit.
